description: The single source of truth for every visual value in PRV AI DJ Studio. Master Prompt #16: nothing downstream may hardcode a colour, a spacing, a radius, a duration or a type style. Swift and JSON outputs are generated from this file by tools/tokengen; the generated files are never edited by hand.

color.description: Dark mode first, as Master Prompt #16 requires. Every token carries both appearances because Master Prompt #8 requires light, dark and high contrast from day one, and retrofitting an appearance is far more expensive than declaring it. Colour never carries meaning alone: every semantic colour below has a paired icon or label in the component that uses it, so that the accessibility requirement and the reactive visuals of Master Prompt #2 do not conflict.

surface.canvas.description: The furthest-back surface. True black in dark mode so that glass layers above it have something to lift away from.

surface.raised.description: Cards and panels resting on the canvas.

surface.glass.description: Translucent material for floating panels and the inspector. Alpha is part of the token because a glass surface without its alpha is not the same material.

accent.primary.description: The product accent, used when no artwork-derived accent is available. Master Prompt #2 requires the accent to follow artwork where one exists; this is the fallback and the brand anchor.

status.danger.description: Clipping, data loss risk, failed operation.

meter.nominal.description: Level metering below the headroom threshold.

meter.clipping.description: True peak at or above the ceiling. Always accompanied by a persistent clip indicator, never colour alone.

ai.onDevice.description: Intelligence running on the device. Master Prompt #26 requires the user to be able to tell at a glance where their data is being processed, so on-device and cloud processing are visually distinct states rather than one undifferentiated 'AI' colour.

ai.cloud.description: Intelligence running on an external service. Paired with an explicit label wherever it appears.

waveform.low.description: Low-frequency energy in the frequency-coloured waveform.

spacing.description: A four-point scale. Every layout is built from these; arbitrary values are a lint failure. Four points is small enough to express tight controls and large enough that the scale stays short enough to remember.

radius.description: Master Prompt #2 calls for large rounded corners. The scale is continuous rather than circular, matching the platform's own curvature.

typography.description: SF Pro Display throughout, as Master Prompt #2 requires. Every style maps to a platform text style so that Dynamic Type scaling is inherited rather than reimplemented. The numeric style exists because BPM, key and timecode change while the user is reading them: without tabular figures the digits shift horizontally on every update, which reads as instability in exactly the values a performer is trusting.

motion.description: Durations and curves. Master Prompt #16 requires motion to communicate state rather than decorate, so the scale is named by intent rather than by length. Every one of these collapses to zero when the system requests reduced motion; the state change still happens, it simply arrives without travel.

instant.description: No animation. What every other token becomes under reduced motion.

long.description: Timeline construction as a mix is generated, where the motion is the explanation.

spring.description: The default for anything the user moved. Physical response makes direct manipulation feel connected to the finger.

elevation.description: Shadow definitions. Kept few and soft: Master Prompt #2 asks for depth, not drama.

opacity.description: Named opacities, so that a disabled control is disabled the same amount everywhere.

blur.description: Material blur radii for the glass surfaces of Master Prompt #2.

pendingGroups.description: Master Prompt #16 names twenty-four token groups. The groups above are the ones with a consumer today. The remainder are declared here rather than invented, because a token defined before anything uses it is a guess that later has to be unpicked. Each lands with the first screen that needs it.
